title: Tracking LRU
description: In a full set, the *least recently used* way is the victim. Read the rank column to name it before it happens.

steps.text: This cache has 2 ways per set and 4 sets, so the set comes from 2 *index* bits. The addresses `0x000`, `0x040`, `0x080` and `0x0C0` all have index `00`: they all compete for the two ways of set 0. The *rank* column says how recently each way was used: 0 is the most recent.
Load `0x000`, then `0x040`. Type each in the address box and press Issue.
steps.hint: Issue `0x000` first. When it has finished, issue `0x040`.

steps.text: Load `0x000` again. Watch the rank column when it hits.
steps.hint: Type `0x000` in the address box and press Issue.

steps.text: Set 0 is full: way 0 holds `0x000` and way 1 holds `0x040`. The next load, `0x080`, also maps to set 0. Which way will it replace?
options: Way 1: it is the least recently used
steps.explain: Way 1. `0x000` was used again a moment ago, so its rank is 0 (most recent) and way 1 has the highest rank, 1. LRU replaces the highest rank, whatever the order of arrival.
steps.hint: Look at the rank column of set 0. Which way reads 1, the least recent?

steps.text: Way 1 now holds `0x080` and has rank 0. `0x040` is gone; `0x000` is still in way 0, now with rank 1.
Next load: `0x0C0`, also set 0. Which way will it replace?
options: Way 0: it is now the least recently used
steps.explain: Way 0. Way 1 was filled by the last load, so it has rank 0, and way 0 has rank 1. `0x000` is evicted: the last time it was used is further back than that of `0x080`.
steps.hint: Which way has the higher number in the rank column now?

steps.text: `0x0C0` took way 0, and `0x000` is out. Neither evicted line had been stored to, so nothing had to be written back. LRU keeps what you used most recently; the next module compares it with a policy that does not.
